column5: NSAIDs can irritate the stomach lining and raise the risk of bleeding in someone with a peptic ulcer or a history of gastrointestinal bleeding. Do not stop a prescribed medicine because of this alert — speak to your doctor or pharmacist.
NSAIDs can reduce blood flow to the kidneys and worsen existing chronic kidney disease. Do not stop a prescribed medicine because of this alert — speak to your doctor or pharmacist.
Some people with asthma react to NSAIDs with worsening breathing symptoms. Do not stop a prescribed medicine because of this alert — speak to your doctor or pharmacist.

Paracetamol is processed by the liver, and cumulative intake carries added risk in liver disease. This matters most when several products contain paracetamol at once. Do not stop a prescribed medicine because of this alert — speak to your doctor or pharmacist.
NSAIDs can raise blood pressure and reduce the effect of some blood pressure medicines. Do not stop a prescribed medicine because of this alert — speak to your doctor or pharmacist.
Decongestants can raise blood pressure. Do not stop a prescribed medicine because of this alert — speak to your doctor or pharmacist.
Sulfonamides can trigger red blood cell breakdown in people with G6PD deficiency. Do not stop a prescribed medicine because of this alert — speak to your doctor or pharmacist.
Some antimalarials can trigger red blood cell breakdown in people with G6PD deficiency. Do not stop a prescribed medicine because of this alert — speak to your doctor or pharmacist.
